history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a CHRISTIAN (Presbyterian) entry, not a Hindu temple. 'Mizo Synod Church' is NOT a documented building name: 'Mizo Synod' is the administrative body of the Mizoram Presbyterian Church (the largest Christian denomination in Mizoram, a direct progeny of the Calvinistic Methodist Church of Wales, and a constituent of the Presbyterian Church of India), headquartered at Mission Veng, Aizawl. The row therefore most likely refers to a Mizoram Synod Presbyterian congregation in Lawngtlai town — the same set of congregations documented under seq 732 ('Presbyterian Church, Lawngtlai': Bazar Veng/Lawngtlai-II, Chandmary, AOC Veng, Bethel, Vengthlang). PROBABLE DUPLICATE of seq 732; the same referent coordinates (22.53135, 92.89763, the Bazar Veng, Lawngtlai-II church below Dokulha Hall) are used. One documented Synod institution in Lawngtlai is the Synod Bookroom Lawngtlai Branch, established 1986, with a new building inaugurated on 6 April 2016. CSV town 'Lawngtlai' is correct; the name is the problem, not the town.

name: Mizo Synod Church
town: Lawngtlai (probable duplicate of seq 732; 'Mizo Synod Church' is not a documented building name)
town_description: Lawngtlai is the district headquarters of Lawngtlai district in southern Mizoram, home to the Lai (Pawi) people. Per the 2011 census the district is 54.19% Christian (Baptist, Presbyterian/Synod and indigenous denominations) and 43.72% Buddhist. The Mizoram Presbyterian Church Synod administers its Lawngtlai congregations through pastor bials, and runs the Synod Bookroom Lawngtlai Branch in the town.

travel.airport: Lengpui Airport (Aizawl), the nearest airport; Lawngtlai is roughly a 5-6 hour drive from Aizawl via Lunglei (verify distance).
travel.railway: No railway station in Lawngtlai; nearest railhead not reliably published (verify) — candidates include Bairabi (Mizoram) and Silchar (Assam).
travel.road: Lawngtlai is connected by road to Aizawl via Lunglei and to Saiha and Chawngte by district roads; buses and shared taxis run from Aizawl and Lunglei (verify).
